usage: Intransitive verb with avere (hanno divorziato); the former partner is introduced by 'da'. Milder 'separarsi' is used for separating without a legal divorce. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: I miei genitori hanno divorziato quando avevo dieci anni.
examples.en: My parents divorced when I was ten.
They are getting divorced after twenty years of marriage.

examples.it: Se divorziassero, i figli resterebbero con la madre.
examples.en: If they divorced, the children would stay with their mother.

usage: Reflexive verb for lying down on a bed, sofa or the grass; the adjective 'sdraiato' means lying down. The beach lounger is 'la sdraio'. Takes essere; regular -are verb.

examples.it: Mi sdraio un po' sul divano.
examples.en: I'm going to lie down on the sofa for a bit.
We lay down on the grass.
Lie down and rest.

en: to toast; to drink a toast
usage: Raising glasses in celebration; what you toast to is introduced by 'a' (brindare alla salute, al nuovo anno). The toast itself is 'il brindisi'; people say 'cin cin' or 'salute'. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Let's drink to good health!
We toasted with sparkling wine.

examples.it: Brinderemo al nuovo anno a mezzanotte.
examples.en: We will toast the new year at midnight.

usage: Acting in a play or film (recitare in un film) and reciting a poem or a prayer. Do not use 'agire', which means to act in the sense of taking action. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: She acts in a small theatre.

examples.it: Ha recitato una poesia di Leopardi.
examples.en: He recited a poem by Leopardi.
Will you act in the film?

usage: Recording audio or video and, in official contexts, registering something. The reflexive 'registrarsi' means to sign up on a website or app. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Registro la lezione con il telefono.
examples.en: I record the lesson with my phone.
They recorded a new album.
Sign up on the website to book.

usage: Installing software and apps as well as appliances and equipment (installare la lavatrice). Regular -are verb; the noun is 'l'installazione'.

examples.en: I am installing the app on my phone.
Did you install the update?
We will install the washing machine tomorrow.

usage: Always with 'a': 'assomiglio a mia madre'. Compound tenses normally use avere, though essere is also found. The reciprocal 'assomigliarsi' means to look alike. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I look like my mother.
As a child he looked like his grandfather.
I don't think she looks like you.

usage: Guessing correctly; 'Indovina!' introduces surprising news, and 'tirare a indovinare' means to take a wild guess. Regular -are verb; the riddle is 'l'indovinello'.

examples.en: Guess who's coming to dinner!
I guessed the answer.

examples.it: Non indovinerai mai chi ho incontrato.
examples.en: You will never guess who I met.

usage: Defending people, ideas and rights; the threat is introduced by 'da'. The reflexive 'difendersi' means to defend oneself. Irregular: passato remoto difesi, participio difeso.

examples.en: The lawyer defends the client.
She defended her friend from the criticism.
We will defend our rights.

usage: Used for the sun, stars and anything bright: 'oggi splende il sole'. Mostly used in simple tenses; the participle 'splenduto' is rare. Regular -ere verb; the adjective is 'splendido'.

examples.en: The sun is shining today.
The stars were shining in the sky.

examples.it: Domani splenderà il sole tutto il giorno.
examples.en: Tomorrow the sun will shine all day.

usage: Used of the sun and moon going down; the sunset is 'il tramonto'. Takes essere (il sole è tramontato). The opposite is 'sorgere'. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: The sun sets at eight.

examples.it: Il sole è tramontato dietro le montagne.
examples.en: The sun set behind the mountains.

examples.it: Quando tramonterà il sole, faremo un falò.
examples.en: When the sun sets, we will make a bonfire.

usage: Used of plants and trees producing flowers, and figuratively of things flourishing. Takes -isc- (fiorisce, fioriscono) and essere in compound tenses (è fiorito). Regular -ire verb.

examples.en: Cherry trees bloom in April.

examples.it: Le rose sono fiorite presto quest'anno.
examples.en: The roses bloomed early this year.
This plant will flower in summer.

usage: What dogs do; the target is introduced by 'a' or 'contro'. Proverb: 'can che abbaia non morde'. Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.en: The dog barks at passers-by.
It barked all night.

examples.it: Se abbaierà ancora, i vicini si arrabbieranno.
examples.en: If it barks again, the neighbours will get angry.

usage: Used for animals and people biting; for insects 'pungere' is more precise, though 'mordere' is common in speech. Irregular: passato remoto morsi, participio morso. 'Mordersi la lingua' means to bite one's tongue.

examples.en: The dog doesn't bite.
A mosquito bit me.

examples.it: Non credo che ti morda, è buono.
examples.en: I don't think it will bite you, it's gentle.

usage: Stroking pets and gently caressing people; figuratively 'accarezzare un'idea' (to toy with an idea). Regular -are verb; the noun is 'la carezza'.

examples.en: I stroke the cat on the sofa.

examples.it: Ha accarezzato il cane con dolcezza.
examples.en: She stroked the dog gently.

examples.it: Accarezzerei il cane, ma ho paura.
examples.en: I would stroke the dog, but I'm scared.

usage: Reflexive verb for diving into water; the place is introduced by 'in' and the starting point by 'da'. Figuratively, 'tuffarsi nel lavoro'. Takes essere; regular -are verb.

examples.en: I dive into the pool.
He dived off the rock.
Would you dive into cold water?

usage: Furnishing and decorating a home; the furniture is 'l'arredamento' and a furnished flat is 'ammobiliato'. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Arrediamo il soggiorno con mobili moderni.
examples.en: We are furnishing the living room with modern furniture.

examples.it: Hanno arredato la casa con gusto.
examples.en: They furnished the house tastefully.

examples.it: Arrederò la camera in bianco e blu.
examples.en: I will furnish the bedroom in white and blue.

usage: Decorating cakes, rooms and Christmas trees; what you use is introduced by 'con'. Regular -are verb; the noun is 'la decorazione'.

examples.it: Decoro la torta con la frutta.
examples.en: I decorate the cake with fruit.
We decorated the Christmas tree.

examples.it: Decoreremo la sala per la festa.
examples.en: We will decorate the hall for the party.

en: to fix; to repair; to adjust
usage: The everyday word for fixing broken things; 'riparare' is slightly more formal. 'Aggiustarsi' colloquially means to sort things out. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: My father fixes everything.
I fixed the broken chair.
I will fix the bike at the weekend.

usage: Wasting water, food, money or time; the noun is 'lo spreco'. Spelling change: h before e/i (sprechi, sprecherò). Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Don't waste water!
We wasted an hour waiting.
If you wasted less food, you would save money.

en: to pick; to pick up; to collect
usage: Picking fruit, flowers or mushrooms, picking things up from the floor, and collecting money or information. Irregular like 'cogliere': raccolgo, raccolsi, raccolto. The harvest is 'la raccolta'.

examples.en: We pick the apples in September.

examples.it: Ha raccolto le chiavi da terra.
examples.en: He picked the keys up off the floor.
We will pick mushrooms in the woods.

usage: Reflexive verb; the imperative 'Calmati!' is very common. Also used of the sea, wind and pain easing. The non-reflexive 'calmare' means to calm someone else. Takes essere; regular -are verb.

examples.en: Calm down, nothing happened.

examples.it: Il bambino si è calmato subito.
examples.en: The child calmed down right away.

examples.it: Mi calmerò quando saprò che stai bene.
examples.en: I will calm down when I know you are all right.

usage: Couples separating (without necessarily divorcing) and people parting; the other person is introduced by 'da'. Takes essere; regular -are verb. The non-reflexive 'separare' means to separate things.

examples.it: I miei si sono separati due anni fa.
examples.en: My parents separated two years ago.
They are splitting up after ten years.
I wouldn't want you to split up.

usage: Having someone stay at your home, or hosting an event. The guest is 'l'ospite' (a word that also means host). Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I am putting a friend up for the weekend.

examples.it: Ci hanno ospitato per una settimana.
examples.en: They put us up for a week.

examples.it: Ti ospiterei volentieri, ma la casa è piccola.
examples.en: I would gladly put you up, but the house is small.

usage: Sticking things with glue and, on a computer, pasting text ('copia e incolla'). The glue is 'la colla'. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Copia il testo e incollalo qui.
examples.en: Copy the text and paste it here.

examples.it: Ho incollato la foto sul quaderno.
examples.en: I glued the photo into the notebook.
We will put up the posters in the centre.

en: to attach (to an email); to enclose
usage: Attaching files to an email or documents to a form; the attachment is 'l'allegato'. In emails: 'in allegato trova...'. Spelling change: h before e/i (alleghi, allegherò).

examples.en: I am attaching the document to the email.
Did you attach your CV?
I will attach the photos to the message.

usage: Takes a direct object with no preposition: 'commentare un post', 'commentare una notizia'. Very common for social media. Regular -are verb; the noun is 'il commento'.

examples.it: Commento sempre le foto degli amici.
examples.en: I always comment on my friends' photos.

examples.it: Il professore ha commentato il mio tema.
examples.en: The teacher commented on my essay.
Would you comment on my post?

en: to block; to jam; to lock
usage: Blocking a phone number or a bank card, roads being blocked, and the reflexive 'bloccarsi' for a computer freezing or a person getting stuck. Spelling change: h before e/i (blocchi, bloccherò).

examples.en: I blocked that number.
The snow is blocking the roads.

examples.it: Se perdi la carta, bloccala subito.
examples.en: If you lose your card, block it immediately.

usage: Public protests (protestare contro una legge) and everyday complaining. The cause is introduced by 'contro' or 'per'. Regular -are verb; the noun is 'la protesta'.

examples.it: Gli studenti protestano contro la riforma.
examples.en: The students are protesting against the reform.
They protested in front of the town hall.
If you protest, maybe they will listen to you.

en: to expire; to be past its date
usage: Used for food, documents, tickets and deadlines. Irregular like 'cadere': passato remoto scaddi, future scadrò. Takes essere (è scaduto); the expiry date is 'la scadenza'.

examples.en: The milk expires tomorrow.
My passport has expired.
The offer will expire at the end of the month.

usage: Renewing documents, subscriptions and contracts (rinnovare il passaporto, l'abbonamento); also renovating a house. Regular -are verb; the noun is 'il rinnovo'.

examples.en: I need to renew my identity card.
We renewed the subscription.
I will renew my passport in January.

usage: Used of the wind (soffia un vento forte) and of people blowing on candles or hot food; 'soffiarsi il naso' means to blow one's nose. Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.en: A strong wind is blowing today.
She blew out the candles.
Blow your nose!

usage: Used on labels and packaging ('contiene glutine') and for boxes, bottles and rooms holding something. Conjugated like 'tenere': contengo, contieni, contiene; contenni; conterrò. Formal 'contenersi' means to control oneself.

examples.it: Questo biscotto contiene latte e uova.
examples.en: This biscuit contains milk and eggs.
The box contained old photos.

examples.it: La nuova sala conterrà duecento persone.
examples.en: The new hall will hold two hundred people.

en: to move; to get a move on
usage: Reflexive form of 'muovere': to move oneself or get around a city; the imperative 'Muoviti!' means 'Hurry up!'. Irregular participle mosso (mi sono mosso), passato remoto mossi. Takes essere.

examples.en: Get a move on, we're late!

examples.it: Non si è mosso dal divano tutto il giorno.
examples.en: He didn't move from the sofa all day.

examples.it: Mi muoverò in bici per la città.
examples.en: I will get around the city by bike.

usage: The person or order obeyed is introduced by 'a' (ubbidire ai genitori). Takes -isc- in the present (ubbidisco, ubbidisci) and avere. The spelling 'obbedire' is equally correct.

examples.en: The dog obeys its owner.
He has always obeyed his parents.
If you don't obey, no TV.

usage: Recognising a person, a voice or a place; what you recognise them by is introduced by 'da'. Also to admit a mistake (riconoscere un errore). Conjugated like 'conoscere': passato remoto riconobbi, participio riconosciuto.

examples.it: Non ti riconosco con questi capelli!
examples.en: I don't recognise you with this hair!
I recognised her by her voice.

examples.it: Riconosceresti la tua città dopo vent'anni?
examples.en: Would you recognise your city after twenty years?

usage: Intransitive, takes avere. Takes -isc- in the present (starnutisco, starnutisci). When someone sneezes Italians say 'Salute!'. The sneeze is 'lo starnuto'.

examples.en: I always sneeze in spring.

examples.it: Ha starnutito tre volte di seguito.
examples.en: He sneezed three times in a row.

examples.it: Se starnutirai ancora, prendi un fazzoletto.
examples.en: If you sneeze again, take a tissue.

usage: Intransitive, takes avere. Takes -isc- in the present (tossisco, tossisci); the noun is 'la tosse' (avere la tosse). Regular -ire verb.

examples.en: I have been coughing for a week.

examples.it: Il bambino ha tossito tutta la notte.
examples.en: The child coughed all night.

examples.it: Se tossirai ancora, chiamiamo il medico.
examples.en: If you keep coughing, we'll call the doctor.

en: to divide; to share; to split
usage: Dividing into parts (dividere in due), sharing something (dividere il conto) and arithmetic division: dividere dieci per due, or dieci diviso due. Irregular passato remoto divisi and participle diviso.

examples.en: Shall we split the bill?

examples.it: Hanno diviso la torta in otto fette.
examples.en: They divided the cake into eight slices.

examples.it: Se dividi dieci per due, ottieni cinque.
examples.en: If you divide ten by two, you get five.

usage: Reflexive verb, very common in the imperative: 'Sbrigati!' (Hurry up!). With a verb it takes 'a' + infinitive. Spelling change: h before e/i (ti sbrighi, mi sbrigherò). Takes essere.

examples.it: Sbrigati, il treno parte tra dieci minuti!
examples.en: Hurry up, the train leaves in ten minutes!

examples.it: Ci siamo sbrigati e siamo arrivati in tempo.
examples.en: We hurried and arrived in time.

examples.it: Se non ti sbrigherai, perderemo l'autobus.
examples.en: If you don't hurry, we will miss the bus.
